title: Mechanistic Investigation of the Androgen Receptor DNA-Binding Domain and Modulation via Direct Interactions with DNA Abasic Sites: Understanding the Mechanisms Involved in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
authors: Xu, Shangze; Kondal, Matthew D; Ahmad, Ayaz; Zhu, Ruidi; Fan, Lanyu; Zaborniak, Piotr; Madden, Katrina S; de Souza, Joao V; Bronowska, Agnieszka K
one_liner_zh: 该文用原子级MD模拟和量子化学计算研究雄激素受体DBD与DNA（含脱碱基损伤）的互作机制，揭示突变和DNA损伤如何调控TF-DNA结合与二聚化，高度契合TF-DNA互作机制建模课题。
abstract: The androgen receptor (AR) is an important drug target in prostate cancer and a driver of castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). A significant challenge in designing effective drugs lies in targeting constitutively active AR variants and, most importantly, nearly all AR variants lacking the ligand-binding domain (LBD). Recent findings show that an AR's constitutive activity may occur in the presence of somatic DNA mutations within non-coding regions, but the role of these mutations remains elusive. The discovery of new drugs targeting CRPC is hampered by the limited molecular understanding of how AR binds mutated DNA sequences, frequently observed in prostate cancer, and how mutations within the protein and DNA regulate AR-DNA interactions. Using atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and quantum mechanical calculations, we focused our efforts on (i) rationalising the role of several activating DBD mutations linked to prostate cancer, and (ii) DBD interactions in the presence of abasic DNA lesions, which frequently occur in CRPC. Our results elucidate the role of mutations within DBD through their modulation of the intrinsic dynamics of the DBD-DNA ternary complex. Furthermore, our results indicate that the DNA apurinic lesions occurring in the androgen-responsive element (ARE) enhance direct AR-DNA interactions and stabilise the DBD homodimerisation interface. Moreover, our results strongly suggest that those abasic lesions may form reversible covalent crosslinks between DNA and lysine residues of an AR via a Schiff base. In addition to providing an atomistic model explaining how protein mutations within the AR DNA-binding domain affect AR dimerisation and AR-DNA interactions, our findings provide insight into how somatic mutations occurring in DNA non-coding regions may activate ARs. These mutations are frequently observed in prostate cancer and may contribute to disease progression by enhancing direct AR-DNA interactions.
abstract_zh: 雄激素受体（AR）是前列腺癌中的重要药物靶点，也是去势抵抗性前列腺癌（CRPC）的驱动因素。设计有效药物的重大挑战在于靶向组成性激活的AR变体，尤其是几乎所有缺乏配体结合域（LBD）的AR变体。近期研究发现，AR的组成性活性可能发生在非编码区域内体细胞DNA突变存在的情况下，但这些突变的作用仍不明确。由于对AR如何结合前列腺癌中常见的突变DNA序列，以及蛋白质和DNA内的突变如何调控AR-DNA相互作用的分子理解有限，靶向CRPC的新药发现受到阻碍。利用原子级分子动力学（MD）模拟和量子力学计算，我们专注于（i）阐明与前列腺癌相关的几种激活型DBD突变的作用，以及（ii）在CRPC中常见的脱碱基DNA损伤存在下的DBD相互作用。我们的结果通过突变对DBD-DNA三元复合物内在动力学的调节，阐明了DBD内突变的作用。此外，我们的结果表明，雄激素反应元件（ARE）中发生的DNA脱嘌呤损伤增强了直接的AR-DNA相互作用，并稳定了DBD同源二聚化界面。更重要的是，我们的结果强烈提示，这些脱碱基损伤可能通过希夫碱在DNA与AR的赖氨酸残基之间形成可逆的共价交联。除了提供解释AR DNA结合域内蛋白质突变如何影响AR二聚化和AR-DNA相互作用的原子模型外，我们的发现还揭示了DNA非编码区域中发生的体细胞突变如何可能激活AR。这些突变在前列腺癌中频繁观察到，并可能通过增强直接的AR-DNA相互作用促进疾病进展。
